title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization
claim: A prediction is decomposed into independent specialized branches whose scores are gated and fused, then trained with a ranking objective.
layout: Left-to-right, input fans out to 3 stacked branches, merges into output
description: A left-to-right pipeline diagram. At the far left a gray box shows the observed graph, with a dashed red edge and a question mark for the candidate link. Arrows fan out to three stacked, color-coded branch boxes inside a dashed container: a blue box (I, Invariant Anchor), an orange box (II, Mixed-Curvature Residual) and a green box (III, Non-Local Geodesic Field). Each box lists its key equations in italic and serif math. Each box has a matching icon to its right: a small graph, hyperbolic and spherical manifolds, and a vector field in a disk. Lines in the branch colors carry the outputs, scaled by λ weights, into a purple 'Gated superposition' box with the combined score formula. A gray 'Ranked edges' box with green bars follows. A red dashed arrow rises from a red 'N-pair ranking loss' box into the fusion box. The eye goes first to the three colored branches.
caption: Overview of Concorde. Link likelihood is decomposed into three structurally decoupled energy branches: a parameter-free spectral anchor on the unperturbed adjacency (global, $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$-invariant), a mixed-curvature residual on $\mathbb{H}\times\mathbb{S}$ with a feature-aware Ollivier--Ricci guardrail (local symmetry-breaking), and a non-local geodesic steering field on $\mathcal{T}\mathbb{H}_c^d$ (bridging topological gaps). Learned scalar gates fuse the branches, and the model is trained with an $N$-pair ranking loss aligned with early-retrieval evaluation.
abstract: Link prediction remains difficult in sparse graphs, where diffusion heuristics lack connectivity and geometric methods suffer spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators. We introduce Concorde, an energy-based framework that resolves this by decomposing link likelihood into three structurally decoupled branches: (i) a parameter-free spectral anchor that establishes permutation-invariant topological stability; (ii) a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable $\mathbb{H}^{d_h}_{c_h} \times \mathbb{S}^{d_s}_{c_s}$ product manifold, regularized by a feature-aware Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy; and (iii) a continuous vector field on the tangent bundle of hyperbolic space for non-local structural alignment across topological gaps. The branches are fused via learned gating and trained with an N-pair ranking loss aligned with retrieval-style evaluation. Across five benchmarks spanning sparse, dense, featureless, and attributed regimes, Concorde establishes state-of-the-art early retrieval precision, nearly doubling P@10% over leading baselines in sparse settings.
